DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Start with the standard shapes and help command, add a command path, mark it runnable, and add its first option token. The workspace itself is the current directory after `cd`, so no workspace switch is needed in the authoring commands.
```powershell meta-cli create --xml .\my-cli.MetaCli --application app-my-cli --standard-cli-shapes --default-help cd .\my-cli.MetaCli meta-cli add-command --id cmd-show --application app-my-cli --name show --token show --description "Show the workspace." meta-cli add-executable-command --id exec-show --command cmd-show meta-cli add-option --parameter-id param-show-workspace --option-id option-show-workspace --executable-command exec-show --name workspace --value-shape shape-path --token-id token-show-workspace --token --workspace --description "Workspace path." ```
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Create a small command surface

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta-cli` authors the command surface that a CLI runtime parses, documents, and binds to handlers. The practical result is one reviewed workspace for applications, commands, options, positional arguments, value shapes, and help.
Create a workspace with the standard shapes and help command, then add a command and mark it executable:
```powershell meta-cli create --xml .\my-cli.MetaCli --application app-my-cli --standard-cli-shapes --default-help cd .\my-cli.MetaCli meta-cli add-command --id cmd-show --application app-my-cli --name show --token show --description "Show the workspace." meta-cli add-executable-command --id exec-show --command cmd-show meta-cli add-option --parameter-id param-show-workspace --option-id option-show-workspace --executable-command exec-show --name workspace --value-shape shape-path --token-id token-show-workspace --token --workspace --description "Workspace path." ```
The runtime, help output, and documentation import all read the same modeled command surface. Behavior is attached to executable-command identities after the public grammar has been authored.
